_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::tsi#2. One HEX8 SOLIDSCATRA cube in free thermal expansion, THEXPANS = 1.2e-05 in all three arms (THEXPANS_RESCALED_BETWEEN_ARMS=1 — one distinct THEXPANS line across the three decks). All-Kelvin (INITTEMP 293, T 393) and all-Celsius (INITTEMP 19.85, T 119.85) describe the same physical state and give the same dispx = 1.2e-03 with the same alpha, both CORRECT and exit 0. That falsifies 'THEXPANS UNITS must match the temperature units': a linear expansion coefficient in 1/K and in 1/degC is the same number, there is nothing to rescale. Mixing the scales (INITTEMP 19.85 with T 393) gives actresult= 4.47779999999999880e-03, off by abs(diff)= 3.27779999999999912e-03, which equals alpha*273.15*L to machine precision (OFFSET_IS_ALPHA_TIMES_273_15=True). The offset the claim measured is real; its cause is the temperature SCALE of INITTEMP versus the thermal field, not THEXPANS. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: put the mixed arm's temperature field back on the same scale as its INITTEMP. The 273.15 offset disappears, dispx returns to 1.2e-03, EXIT_MIXED becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
